title: Day 25 · 系统设计面试 (System Design Interview) — System Design
title_en: Day 25 · System Design Interview — System Design

questions.question: 系统设计面试题是「设计 Twitter」，只有 45 分钟。哪种开场最能体现资深候选人的判断力？
options: 先澄清需求，主动提出只聚焦发推和 home timeline 两条最有取舍张力的路径，并征得同意
直接画出包含 CDN、Redis、Kafka 的完整架构图，节省时间留给深挖
尽量把搜索、广告、私信、trending、媒体转码等功能都列出来逐一设计，展示自己对整个系统的全面理解
只设计一个最简单的发帖 CRUD 服务，确保在时间内把它做到完美
questions.explanation: 开放题的第一动作是把题收敛成可设计的题：选 1–2 个有 trade-off 张力的核心功能讲透，深度永远优于广度，并给出理由征得 buy-in——这同时传递判断力和沟通信号。贪多会没有深度，直接堆组件像报菜名，只做 CRUD 又显得缺乏系统思维。
questions.question_en: The system design prompt is "design Twitter," with 45 minutes. Which opening best signals senior-level judgment?
options_en: Clarify requirements, then propose focusing only on posting and the home timeline—the paths with the most trade-off tension—explaining why and getting the interviewer's agreement
Immediately draw a full architecture with CDN, Redis, and Kafka to save time for the deep dive
List and design as many features as possible—search, ads, DMs, trending, media transcoding—to show a comprehensive grasp of the whole system
Design only the simplest post-CRUD service and make sure it's perfect within the time
questions.explanation_en: The first move on an open problem is to turn it into a designable one: pick one or two core features with real trade-off tension and go deep—depth beats breadth—while giving reasons and getting buy-in, which signals both judgment and communication. Covering everything leaves no depth, stacking components is just naming dishes, and a bare CRUD service shows no systems thinking.

questions.question: 在系统设计面试中被问到消息队列选型，下面哪种回答最接近满分的 trade-off 表达？
options: 要支持 replay，所以选 Kafka 而非 RabbitMQ，代价是运维更复杂；不需要 replay 就改选后者
Kafka 和 RabbitMQ 各有各的优缺点，具体用哪个最好还是要看团队的偏好和熟悉程度
用 Kafka，因为它是业界最成熟、吞吐量最高、社区最活跃的消息队列，大厂基本都在用，选它不会出错
先用 Kafka 把系统跑起来，之后遇到具体问题再根据线上实际情况调整和替换
questions.explanation: 满分表达要包含约束、被淘汰的替代方案、选择的理由、付出的代价，最后再说约束一变会改选什么——最后这句是 staff 信号。只给结论是零信号；说「各有优缺点」没有做出决策；「先用再调」也没有讲清放弃了什么。
questions.question_en: Asked to choose a message queue in a system design interview, which answer comes closest to a top-scoring trade-off explanation?
options_en: Because replay is needed, choose Kafka over RabbitMQ at the cost of heavier ops; without replay, switch to RabbitMQ
Kafka and RabbitMQ each have their pros and cons; which is best depends on the team's preferences and familiarity
Use Kafka, because it's the industry's most mature, highest-throughput queue with the most active community—nearly every big company uses it, so you can't go wrong
Start with Kafka to get things running, then adjust or swap it later based on real production issues
questions.explanation_en: A top answer states the constraints, the rejected alternative, the reason for the choice, the cost paid, and finally what you'd pick if the constraints changed—that last part is the staff-level signal. A bare conclusion carries no signal, "each has pros and cons" makes no decision, and "adjust later" never says what you're giving up.

questions.question: 面试官刚给设计题加了一个新约束：一致性要从最终一致改成强一致。此时怎样处理「出声推理」最合适？
options: 先说出一个结论稳住局面，之后发现不对再悄悄修改
保持沉默，直到在脑子里想出完整的最终方案为止，再一次性把正确答案讲给面试官听
立刻开口，边想边说，把每个闪过的念头都讲出来，避免冷场
先花 20–30 秒在白板上组织要点，形成有结构的小结论，再讲推理路径
questions.explanation: 出声推理的目的是暴露有结构的思考，不是填满每一秒沉默。面对新约束或硬问题，明确说「让我想 30 秒」再开口更显资深；语无伦次的流式输出反而暴露思路混乱。但全程沉默、只给答案又拿不到沟通分——沉默用来组织，出声用来呈现。
questions.question_en: The interviewer has just added a new constraint: consistency must change from eventual to strong. How should you handle "thinking out loud" at this point?
options_en: Blurt out a conclusion to hold the floor, then quietly revise it later if it's wrong
Stay silent until you've worked out the complete final design in your head, then present the right answer all at once
Start talking immediately and voice every passing thought, so there's no awkward silence
Spend 20–30 seconds organizing points on the whiteboard into a small structured conclusion, then narrate the reasoning
questions.explanation_en: Thinking aloud exists to expose structured thinking, not to fill every second. With a new constraint or hard question, saying "let me think for 30 seconds" and then speaking reads as more senior; a rambling stream of thoughts exposes confusion. But silence throughout with only a final answer forfeits communication credit—use silence to organize, speech to present.
